change.title: ao-replay/9055-r1
change.description: fix(chat): take files while an archived chat restores
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

findings.title: Remove button on a file taken during an optimistic send is enabled but does nothing
findings.body: This change lets a file be attached while an optimistic send is pending (`attachBlocked` is false when `optimisticSend`), and the chip for it renders because `stripAttachments` keeps files that were not part of the send (line 930-931). The chip's X is now enabled (`disabled={Boolean(disabled) || queuedEditRecovery || attachBlocked}`), but its `onClick` still begins with `if (submitInFlight.current) return;` (line 2680). `submitInFlight` is set to the `performSubmit` promise at line 1804, and that promise awaits `onSend` for the whole send (lines 2180-2195), so it is non-null for exactly the window in which `optimisticSend` is true. Clicking X on the new chip therefore silently does nothing. Before this PR the button was disabled in that window (`draftMutationPending`), so the guard was never reached. The new test does not click Remove. Fix: let the click through when `optimisticSend` (as `acceptsFiles` and `onDragOver` already do with `submitInFlight.current && !optimisticSend`), and add a test that removes a file taken during a pending send.

findings.title: restoresInFlight entry is deleted unconditionally, so an older restore can drop a newer one's entry
findings.body: `restoresInFlight.set(key, restore)` overwrites any existing entry for the session, and the `finally` deletes the key regardless of whether the map still holds this call's promise. Two overlapping `resume` mutations for the same session (for example a send and the explicit resume action, which both go through `resume.mutateAsync`, lines 1706 and 1764) would let the first one to finish remove the key while the second restore is still running. A file staged in that gap posts to `/attachments` before the worktree is back, which is the failure this map is meant to prevent. Guard the delete with `if (restoresInFlight.get(key) === restore)`, or reuse the existing entry instead of starting a second restore.

findings.title: Does a Cloud session's restore finishing mean its worker can take staged files?
findings.body: `SessionChatSurface` now offers staging as soon as `resumingAgent` is true, and `useStageAttachments` posts right after the restore promise settles. For a Cloud session, `useRestoreSession` returns success once the control plane has accepted the request and the session flips to "reviving" (useRestoreSession.ts:72-85). The previous comment said an archived Cloud chat took files only once it was back. Is the attachments endpoint ready at that point for a Cloud session, or can the POST fail while the sandbox is re-provisioning? The new tests only cover the local restore path.

findings.title: Waiting on the restore ignores the staging abort signal
findings.body: `await restoresInFlight.get(...)` does not observe the `signal` passed to `useStageAttachments`. If the user removes the chip while the restore is running, staging stays parked until the restore ends. It then POSTs the file to the worktree even though the caller cancelled it, leaving an orphaned staged file. Check `signal?.aborted` (or race the wait against the signal) after the await and before the POST.

contracts.action: Take a file for the next message while an optimistic send is pending (paste, drop, picker, Add menu)
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous gates (onPaste, acceptsDroppedFiles, picker onChange) blocked on submitInFlight and draftMutationPending. The new acceptsFiles() relaxes both only when optimisticSend is true.
contracts.before_after: Before: attaching was blocked for the whole send. After: allowed during an optimistic send. The sent files are filtered out of the strip by id (line 929-931). applyAcceptedDraftResult keeps in-flight staging by skipping fileAttachments.clear() while preparing (line 1174). clearAcceptedChatComposer keeps composer.attachments when delivery.draft is set (chat-drafts.ts:1665), and persistAttachments strips sent ids (lines 732-734).
contracts.visible_effect: The new chip shows during the send and survives acceptance. Its X is enabled but the click handler no-ops while submitInFlight is set (finding at line 2692).
contracts.failure_mode: If the send fails, existing recovery in chat-drafts.ts:1150-1158 merges or conflicts with the new composer attachments. That code is not changed here and was not traced fully.
contracts.open_question: What does the failed-send recovery do with attachments added during the send?

contracts.action: Stage attachments while an archived chat restores; staging waits for the in-flight restore
contracts.equivalent_path: The resume mutationFn (lines 1249-1268) runs restore, then invalidateSession. Staging now waits on the same restoresInFlight promise before the POST.
contracts.before_after: Before: staging was offered only after the session was active. After: offered while resumingAgent, and the POST is held until the restore settles. A failed restore rejects staging with SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED and the POST is never made (covered by the new test).
contracts.visible_effect: The file chip appears once the restore finishes. On a failed restore the composer's existing staging-failure notice shows. The file goes with the next message, not the one that triggered the restore.
contracts.failure_mode: Concurrent restores for one key can clear each other's entry (finding at line 1262). The abort signal is ignored during the wait. Cloud restore readiness was not verified.
contracts.open_question: Is the attachments endpoint usable for a Cloud session immediately after restoreCloudSession resolves?

summary: The restore-wait design in `useConversation.ts` holds up: it waits on the in-flight restore before staging, and a failed restore blocks staging. One real bug: the Remove button on a file taken during an optimistic send is enabled but its click handler returns early, so it does nothing. Smaller concerns are the unconditional `restoresInFlight` delete with overlapping restores, the abort signal being ignored during the wait, and an open question about Cloud restore readiness. The new tests cover the happy path and a failed restore, but not removing a file taken during a send.
